responsibilities.name: Weekly Executive Update
responsibilities.instruction: Produce this week's Weekly Executive Update to structure the 30-minute weekly executive sync. Read your source folder, the designated meetings, the output folder and the brand-guide doc id from core memory (do not look up a 'process' document; do not use the calendar). For each designated meeting read its most recent notes (from a folder, the '- Transcript' doc, NOT the '- Recording' video; from a direct doc id, that doc) and SAVE its full text to a working file; gather every designated source you can, and if one is unavailable this week note it and proceed with the rest. Then synthesize a COMPLETE briefing — agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due table — where every section carries real content drawn from the transcripts (no empty or placeholder sections). Deliver it as ONE branded Google Doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date>' in the output folder (updating this week's doc if it already exists; ids copied verbatim) and report the shareable link plus the section headings you read back.
responsibilities.success_criteria: This week's Weekly Executive Update exists as a branded Google Doc TITLED 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date, YYYY-MM-DD>' (not the legacy 'Weekly Executive Brief', and using today's real date) in the exec-summaries output folder, and its shareable link is reported. As evidence, the agent READ THE FINISHED DOCUMENT BACK and reported the exact section headings AND confirmed each has real, non-empty body content synthesized from the transcripts — an empty-section or placeholder document does NOT satisfy this. Required sections: agenda-at-a-glance, State of the Week, per-area status with blockers, Decisions to Lock, and an owner/action/due Action Items table. Sourced from the designated weekly meetings that were available this week (any designated meeting with no occurrence, or an unreadable source, is NOTED in the briefing rather than blocking the work); no non-designated meeting is used; acronyms normalized (e.g. SOC 2); and exactly ONE doc for this week exists (this week's doc was updated, not duplicated).

context.purpose: Leadership runs a 30-minute weekly executive sync and needs one reliable, skimmable briefing, built the same way every week from that week's meeting notes.
process: READ MEMORY (do this first, with core-memory-read): load this deployment's weekly-exec specifics from your core memory (category resources) — the shared meeting-notes SOURCE folder id, the designated source meetings (each is either a recurring FOLDER id or a direct DOC id — memory says which), the exec-summaries OUTPUT folder id, and the brand-guide doc id. These live in memory; 'the process' is THIS list of steps, not a document to look up. If a required id is missing from memory, say so and stop rather than guessing or using the calendar.

GATHER — full text of each source, saved to the workspace: for EACH designated meeting, get its MOST RECENT notes and save the FULL text to a file in your working directory (docs-cat <id> --out <meeting>.txt). Capturing full text to disk is REQUIRED so the document body is written from the full transcripts, not a lossy summary. Per source: if memory gives a recurring FOLDER, list it, pick the single most recent occurrence by date, and read ONLY the Google Doc whose name ends '- Transcript' (SKIP the '- Recording' video/mp4, which is not text); if memory gives a direct DOC id, read that doc itself. Use ONLY your designated meetings; EXCLUDE every other meeting in the space. Gather every designated source you CAN — but if one has no occurrence this week or cannot be read, NOTE that in one line and PROCEED with the sources you have; do NOT block, and do NOT retry a missing source more than once.

SYNTHESIZE from the SAVED files (never from a summary): read the saved files back and distill them into a content JSON in the docs-create-branded --content format — an array of section objects such as {"type":"heading","level":2,"text":"..."}, {"type":"paragraph","text":"..."}, {"type":"bullet_list","items":["..."]}, {"type":"table","headers":[...],"rows":[[...]]}. EVERY heading MUST be followed by paragraph/bullet/table sections carrying the ACTUAL substance from the transcripts — specific decisions, owners, risks, dates, numbers. NEVER emit a heading with no body, and never use placeholder text; an empty or placeholder section is a FAILURE. Include exactly these top-level sections in order: 'Agenda-at-a-Glance' (the segments + rough time boxes summing to ~30 min), 'State of the Week' (what shipped, biggest risk, focus, binding constraint), per-area status (group the areas that appear in the notes, blockers inline), 'Decisions to Lock', and an owner/action/due Action Items table (5-10 top items). Normalize acronyms (e.g. 'Sock 2' -> SOC 2). About three pages.

DELIVER in one step, from the JSON you built: FIRST list the OUTPUT folder; if a doc titled 'Weekly Executive Update - <today's date>' already exists there, UPDATE that one (do not create a second doc). Otherwise create it with docs-create-branded --title "Weekly Executive Update - <TODAY's actual date, YYYY-MM-DD>" --content <your content json file> --brand-doc <brand-guide id from memory> --folder <output folder id from memory>. Use TODAY's real date in the title — never a meeting date or a future date; the title must read 'Weekly Executive Update - <date>' (not 'Brief'). Copy every id EXACTLY from memory (verbatim).

VERIFY with evidence: read the finished doc back and report (a) the section headings AND, for each, that it has real non-empty body content — an empty-section doc does NOT count as done; (b) the source transcripts you used (and any designated source you had to skip); (c) the shareable link. That read-back is the proof.
